transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-15
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Alex Romero (CTO, Orion), Priya Singh (Head of MLOps), Daniel Park (SRE)

Summary (auto): Initial discovery focused on dedicated/reserved capacity for inference. Customer evaluating tradeoffs between hosted, dedicated and private. Interested in guaranteed throughput, isolation, burst strategy and security/compliance requirements.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm maya from redwood, with liam our solutions engineer, how's it going?
[00:12] Alex: good thanks maya, quick note we joined from the office in nyc, little tight on time so we want to focus on expected throughput and sec requirements, i'm alex cto of orion.
[00:22] Maya: perfect, goal for today is to understand your workloads, traffic patterns, what you need from dedicated vs hosted, and next steps for a pilot. liam will cover performance and burst strategies.
[00:35] Liam: hi folks, liam here, i'll jump in around benchmarks, node types, autoscale, etc. feel free to interrupt.
[00:44] Priya: thanks, we run two main inference workloads: a document summarization/chat assist for customer ops (low latency preferred) and a nightly batch reranking job for risk models (higher throughput, can be async).
[01:02] Daniel: and from infra, we need isolation - customer data can't leave our environment for the risk rerank, probably need dedicated capacity or private deployment.
[01:15] Maya: got it. when you say isolation - is this regulatory/data residency or internal policy?
[01:22] Priya: a mix. for certain PII we need tenant isolation and audit logs. also SOC2 is a must.
[01:29] Alex: timeline is Q4 pilot ideally. reserved capacity for production next year.
[01:36] Liam: ok makes sense. quick q: what are your qps and latency targets for the chat assist and the reranker?
[01:44] Priya: chat ~150 concurrent users during peak, roughly 20 qps on average, 60 qps peaks. we'd like p95 latency under 300ms for short prompts.
[01:58] Alex: rerank runs nightly jobs, 200k docs, want to keep job under 2 hours. cost is a big factor here.
[02:08] Liam: great, so two different patterns - online low-latency small inference vs batch high-throughput. dedicated is a good fit because you can reserve GPU pools tuned for each workload.
[02:20] Maya: to clarify options briefly: hosted is fastest to start but shared, dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools with predictable throughput and isolation within a Redwood-managed pool, and private VPC/on-prem gives you control of the control-plane and networking if you need it.
[02:36] Priya: the difference between dedicated and private - is dedicated still in redwood's tenancy? we need to understand data flow.
[02:44] Liam: yes dedicated is in Redwood's infra but isolated customer pools, data at rest encryption and audit logs. private (VPC or on-prem) hands you the control plane and networking so egress doesn't leave your cloud region and you can integrate with KMS/HSM. sometimes customers start with dedicated then move to private for compliance.
[03:03] Daniel: ok that matches our expectations, question on burst - can dedicated handle spiky traffic? we have occasional pushes in the chat workload when marketing campaigns run.
[03:13] Liam: dedicated supports configurable autoscaling and burst capacity but it's bounded by the reserved pool plus a configurable burst bucket. you can set policies to allow overflow to hosted or to queue requests. the buffer size and burst duration depend on your reserved commit.
[03:26] Maya: common pattern is to reserve baseline for steady QPS and allow burst to hosted or burst nodes if you want low-latency during campaign spikes. if you need strict isolation for all traffic, we'd recommend Private to avoid any overflow to hosted.
[03:44] Alex: hm, overflow to hosted is a problem for us for the rerank batch - must stay in our pool. but for chat maybe overflow to hosted is okay?
[03:54] Priya: exact, yes rerank must remain isolated. chat can be flexible.
[04:01] Liam: then we can propose a hybrid: dedicated pool for rerank (no overflow) and a mixed pool for chat with burst-to-hosted allowed. also you can throttle or degrade quality via smaller model in burst to keep latency.
[04:16] Daniel: what's the typical node and GPU sizing? nvidia a100, h100? we're on aws and gcp.
[04:26] Liam: we recommend H100s for high perf LLMs and A100 for cost-sensitive workloads - depends on model quantization and sequence lengths. for chat short seqs H100 gives better latency; for batched rerank you can get good throughput on A100 with optimized kernels.
[04:41] Alex: can you share numbers? p95 latencies and tokens per second?
[04:46] Liam: i'll share our benchmark sheet - but rough rule: with H100 we can push p95 100-200ms on short prompts for mid-size models at moderate qps per GPU, and A100 can do several thousand tokens/sec when batched for rerank. numbers vary with model/quantization.
[05:01] Maya: we'll include a model-specific benchmark for the prompt set you give us. liam will ask for your sample prompts.
[05:08] Priya: we can provide 20 representative prompts for chat and a sample rerank batch.
[05:14] Alex: about quantization - do you support INT8/4-bit? we want lower cost for rerank.
[05:20] Liam: yes, Redwood runtime supports quantized variants and we recommend quantization for rerank throughput. we also provide recommendations per workload in Redwood Optimize. caveat: some quantization can affect quality so we usually run evals on your prompt set.
[05:34] Daniel: security - KMS integration, SSO, audit logs? do you support customer-managed keys?
[05:41] Liam: yes, we integrate with cloud KMS for private deployments and for dedicated we offer encryption at rest; for customer-managed keys on dedicated we can do KMS bring-your-own-key for certain configs, we'll need a privacy/crypto review. SSO/SAML and RBAC supported.
[05:57] Priya: SOC2 attestation paper? we need certs and pen-test reports.
[06:01] Maya: we'll share our SOC2 report and security pack. LINK: https://redwood.example.com/security/soc2 and i'll attach the docs.
[06:10] Alex: thanks. two more things - latency SLOs and fair usage? if we reserve, what guarantees do we get?
[06:18] Liam: for dedicated we offer SLA-backed uptime and we can define latency SLOs for baselined workloads; throughput is bounded by committed GPUs. operationally we expose tracing and token-level cost/latency in the console so you can see hotspots.
[06:33] Daniel: how do upgrades/rollouts work? we need stable model versions and canaries.
[06:38] Liam: Redwood supports version pinning and canary rollouts; you can configure automatic fallback to a compatible model variant if a rollout regresses.
[06:46] Priya: ok cool. cost model - reserved commit vs on-demand, pricing per GPU and discounts?
[06:54] Maya: pricing for dedicated is a reserved monthly commit (we'll show 3-tier options) plus usage for burst if used. we'll send detail.
[07:02] Alex: pilot design idea: 4-week pilot - we test chat and rerank, run shadow traffic and benchmark. can you support that?
[07:09] Maya: yes common. pilot typically includes baseline configuration, benchmarks, support from SE and an evaluation plan. we can scope the pilot to include a small dedicated pool for rerank and a mixed pool for chat.
[07:22] Liam: operational note: for rerank you can use larger batch sizes to amortize cost; for chat we tune batching thresholds and KV caching for context reuse to reduce tokens.
[07:34] Priya: what's KV cache? we haven't used that term.
[07:37] Liam: kv cache is the llama/gpt style attention key-value cache that we keep warm across requests to avoid recomputing prefixes; it's big win for chat low latency and cost. sometimes transcribed as 'k v cash' in notes heh.
[07:49] Alex: are there any limits on model choice? can we bring our own model artifacts?
[07:55] Liam: yes we support bringing models; Redwood also has a model catalog and we can import customer models. for private/on-prem we can run customer-supplied containers if needed (air-gapped).
[08:07] Daniel: networking for private - do you do a control plane handshake over internet or via private link?
[08:12] Liam: private options include VPC peering or PrivateLink-type setup; control plane can be customer-managed. we'll do a deeper technical call on network topology if you go that route.
[08:23] Priya: ok great. can you explain burst policy in more detail - specifically how long bursts can run and cost implications?
[08:30] Liam: bursts are configured by a burst bucket and max burst nodes; typical burst windows are minutes to an hour depending on capacity; cost is on-demand for burst usage unless you have a special agreement. we can also configure auto-throttle or degrade to smaller models to save cost.
[08:45] Maya: example real customers reserve 60-70% capacity for baseline and enable burst for marketing spikes; others reserve 100% and use private for total isolation.
[08:55] Alex: we like the hybrid idea. for rerank, reserve 100% (no overflow). for chat reserve baseline for 80% of normal and allow burst-to-hosted.
[09:05] Priya: for SLOs, can we set hard p95 goals and get alerting?
[09:09] Liam: yes, Redwood Console provides per-route p95 and alerting hooks; we can configure regression alerts tied to prompt set/eval.
[09:18] Maya: we'll prepare a proposed architecture diagram: two pools - rerank dedicated with no overflow; chat dedicated pool with burst-to-hosted allowed; and a potential private pilot if you need keys in-vpc.
[09:29] Alex: second question: what's the onboarding time for dedicated- how long to spin up reserved GPU pools?
[09:35] Liam: typical lead time is 2-4 weeks for reserved capacity depending on GPU availability and region; private can take longer based on networking approvals. pilot can be faster if we use available capacity.
[09:47] Priya: any constraints about cloud provider? we prefer AWS in us-east-1 for latency.
[09:52] Liam: we operate in multiple cloud regions; we'll confirm node availability in us-east-1 when we send the proposal.
[09:59] Daniel: about telemetry - can we get token-level logs? any retention constraints?
[10:03] Maya: yes you can get detailed tracing and token-level cost breakdowns; retention is configurable and extended retention is an add-on. we'll include options.
[10:13] Alex: okay let's talk numbers - what would 4-week pilot cost look like roughly?
[10:18] Maya: rough back-of-the-envelope: small dedicated pool for rerank (2-4 GPUs) plus a chat pool (2 GPUs baseline, plus burst) - pilot cost depends on instance types. we'll put concrete numbers in the pricing sheet.
[10:34] Priya: one more compliance question - do you support customer audit logs and export for compliance teams?
[10:40] Liam: yes audit logs and SIEM integration available, we can export logs to your S3 or SIEM.
[10:47] Alex: good. any show-stopper limitations we should know?
[10:50] Liam: main limits are GPU availability in region and model compatibility for extreme quantization. also if you require zero external egress for all traffic that pushes towards private/on-prem.
[10:59] Priya: on the model side we'll send a sample of our rerank model and chat prompts; we might want to bring our own finetuned model to evaluate.
[11:07] Maya: that's fine. we'll add model import steps to the pilot scope.
[11:11] Alex: ok action items recapped?
[11:14] Maya: i'll send pricing and node configs; liam sends benchmark sheet and will request prompt set; priya/daniel will send what is needed from Orion.
[11:23] Daniel: i'll check with infra on VPC/peering constraints.
[11:27] Priya: we'll try to get prompts by end of week.
[11:31] Maya: great. next meeting - technical deep-dive if pilot moves forward, otherwise we'll touch base after you review docs.
[11:40] Alex: thanks everyone, that's helpful.
[11:43] Maya: thanks all, bye.

Notes on transcription: small name mislabels and 'kv cache' heard as 'k v cash' in a few spots. occasional filler words removed for readability.
